spontaneous and provoked epileptiform-like electrographic activity
brain anatomy and neuronal circuit organization unaffected

impaired integrin-KCNB1 complex signaling in R312H brains

higher c-Fos in arcuate neurons that did not increase with leptin stimulation

biological.citation: Kang et al. 2019/2020 - Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
biological.summary: Kcnb1 G379R knock-in mice (CRISPR/Cas9) showed hyperactivity, repetitive behaviors, spontaneous and induced seizures, increased proconvulsant sensitivity, and abnormal interictal EEG. Brain immunohistochemistry showed genotype-dependent changes in Kv2.1, Kv2.2 and AMIGO-1 expression. In HEK293T cells, G379R failed to induce ER-plasma membrane junctions and reduced WT-induced junctions, consistent with a dominant-negative effect.

biological.citation: De novo KCNB1 mutations in infantile epilepsy inhibit repetitive neuronal firing (PMID: 26477325)
biological.summary: Kv2.1 encodes the major delayed rectifier current in pyramidal neurons. Exome data from 437 infantile epilepsy patients identified de novo R306C and G401R variants. R306C disrupted voltage-sensor sensitivity and cooperativity, while G401R abolished endogenous Kv2 currents in transfected pyramidal neurons (dominant-negative). Both mutants inhibited repetitive neuronal firing.

biological.citation: Molecular mechanisms underlying the apoptotic effect of KCNB1 K+ channel oxidation (PMID: 23275378)
biological.summary: Oxidized KCNB1 forms Cys73-dependent disulfide oligomers that accumulate in the plasma membrane because of defective dynamin 2-dependent endocytosis. KCNB1 localizes to lipid rafts, and the oligomers disrupt raft integrity and trigger apoptosis via c-Src/JNK signaling. The oxidation-resistant C73A variant is cytoprotective.

biological.citation: Toxic role of K+ channel oxidation in mammalian brain (PMID: 22442077)
biological.summary: KCNB1 is abundant in cortex and hippocampus, and its oxidant-induced oligomers are ~10-fold more abundant in old than young mouse brain and are increased in 3xTg-AD mice. The C73A variant protected neuronal cells from Aβ1-42-induced apoptosis. In C. elegans, the homolog C113S-KVS-1 protected neurons from apoptosis induced by ectopic human Aβ1-42.

biological.citation: Stress-induced translation of KCNB1 contributes to the enhanced synaptic transmission of the lateral habenula (PMID: 38193032)
biological.summary: Phosphorylated ribosome capture showed KCNB1 translation/expression increased in lateral habenula neurons after acute stress. shRNA knockdown of Kcnb1 altered basal firing patterns and prevented stress-induced enhancement of synaptic strength. It did not rescue despair-like behavior.

biological.citation: Cdyl Deficiency Brakes Neuronal Excitability and Nociception through Promoting Kcnb1 Transcription in Peripheral Sensory Neurons (PMID: 35119221)
biological.summary: The epigenetic factor CDYL deposits H3K27me3 at the Kcnb1 intron and silences Kcnb1 transcription in sensory neurons. CDYL loss increases Kv2.1 current density in DRG and reduces excitability and nociception. Kv2.1 knockdown reverses the pain-related phenotypes of Cdyl-deficient mice.

biological.citation: Role of KCNB1 in the prognosis of gliomas and autophagy modulation (PMID: 28144039)
biological.summary: KCNB1 expression was associated with favorable overall and progression-free survival in glioma datasets (CGGA, GSE16011, REMBRANDT). KCNB1 induced autophagy through the ERK pathway, increased apoptosis, and reduced proliferation and invasion of glioma cells. In vivo it inhibited tumor growth and increased survival.

biological.citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation (PMID: 40332468)
biological.summary: In larval zebrafish, kcnb1 is expressed in neurons, oligodendrocytes and microglia across the CNS. kcnb1+/- and kcnb1-/- CRISPR knockouts showed impaired swimming, epilepsy-like activity, PTZ hypersensitivity, increased bdnf and c-Fos, and GABA dysregulation. Human Kv2.1 WT DNA restored the phenotypes.

biological.citation: Induction of stable ER-plasma-membrane junctions by Kv2.1 potassium channels (PMID: 25908859)
biological.summary: Clustered, non-conducting Kv2.1 induces stable ER-plasma membrane junctions in HEK293 cells and cultured hippocampal neurons, shown by TIRF and electron microscopy. The clusters act as membrane-trafficking hubs and Ca2+ signaling scaffolds. Glutamate exposure disperses the clusters and retracts the cortical ER.

biological.citation: A KCNB1 gain of function variant causes developmental delay and speech apraxia but not seizures (PMID: 36618935)
biological.summary: The de novo P17T variant in the Kv2.1 N-terminus increased current, shifted steady-state inactivation rightward, and reduced sensitivity to guanxitoxin-1E in whole-cell patch-clamp recordings. This gain of function is associated with developmental delay but no seizures.

biological.citation: ASHG 2014 - De Novo KCNB1 Mutations in Epileptic Encephalopathy
biological.summary: Family-based genome sequencing found de novo KCNB1 missense mutations in three epileptic encephalopathy patients. Functional studies showed that the mutation caused loss of ion selectivity and a gain of depolarizing inward cation conductance in Kv2.1.
